einzeiler: Melissa Auf der Maur talks about her memoir, Hole, and the Smashing Pumpkins.
kurzfassung: Musician and author Melissa Auf der Maur discusses her memoir, Even the Good Girls Will Cry, reflecting on the intense period of joining Hole in 1994 and later playing with the Smashing Pumpkins. She shares insights into the complex personalities of Courtney Love and Billy Corgan, her family background as the child of journalists, and her transition into motherhood and running an arts center. The conversation also touches on her ongoing creative work and the enduring legacy of 90s alternative rock.
stichpunkte: Melissa Auf der Maur released her memoir, Even the Good Girls Will Cry, detailing her turbulent time joining Hole in 1994.
She reflects on the heavy grief, addiction, and intense media scrutiny surrounding Courtney Love following the deaths of Kurt Cobain and Kristen Pfaff.
The memoir aims to humanize Courtney Love by providing context about her neglected childhood and the systemic family pain.
Auf der Maur describes music as the most sacred act in the universe and credits it with saving Courtney Love's life during the 1994 tour.
After leaving Hole, she joined the Smashing Pumpkins just as Darcy Wretzky departed, marking another intense era with a demanding frontman, Billy Corgan.
She discusses her parents' background as prominent counterculture journalists in Canada and how their worldview helped her navigate the music industry.
Leaving the touring life behind 15 years ago, she became a mother and co-founded Basilica Hudson, an independent arts center in upstate New York.
She expresses newfound closeness with both Courtney Love and Billy Corgan, noting they are happier and more considerate today.

clips.hook: Stepping onto the stage amidst tragedy and hostility
clips.text: Shortly after joining the band in the wake of multiple tragedies, the bassist performed before a complex audience ranging from devoted fans to hostile critics blaming them for recent events.

clips.hook: Generational trauma behind a larger-than-life persona
clips.text: The public figure's aggressive demeanor stemmed from a background of neglect and multiple generations of motherless daughters who lacked the ability to love.

clips.hook: The music industry turning magic into a corporate product
clips.text: The commercialization of alternative rock tested the boundaries of authenticity, transforming raw artistic expression into merchandise and consumer goods.

clips.hook: Surviving in the shadow of two impossible personalities
clips.text: A fellow artist praised her ability to maintain her own identity while working closely alongside two of the most difficult and demanding figures of that musical era.

clips.hook: An early attempt to disconnect crowds from their phones
clips.text: When launching an independent music festival over a decade ago, the organizer began hand-writing signs encouraging attendees to leave their mobile devices in their cars.

beschreibung:
This week, hosts Jim DeRogatis and Greg Kot talk with musician and author Melissa Auf der Maur. In 1994, Melissa was suddenly thrust into the spotlight when she joined Hole as a bassist for the “Live Through This” world tour. They talk about Melissa’s memoir, Even the Good Girls Will Cry, and about Courtney Love, Billy Corgan and the power of music. Jim and Greg also review the new album from Steve Lacy.
